description: proj_cqr's cuSOLVER batched potrf+trsm (CholeskyQR2) is ~12ms = shape 11's 2nd-biggest stage and currently library-locked. A sibling found a SINGLE-CTA-per-matrix fused Cholesky is occupancy-bound (1 CTA/SM from the 176KB k*k factor) and lost 30-40x; but the untried variant is a WARP-PER-MATRIX (or few-warps-per-matrix) batched Cholesky+trsm for the k=300 blocks across the 640-matrix batch — many small factorizations at high occupancy, the way cuSOLVER's own batched potrf gets speed, but fused so the k*k factor stays resident between potrf and the tall trsm (removing the HBM round-trip a sibling measured). Small k=300 per-matrix Cholesky is ~O(k^3/3) — with a warp or two per matrix and 640 matrices, occupancy is high. Targets the launch/HBM-round-trip + library-call overhead of the CQR2; keep the residual gate + cuSOLVER fallback + orthogonality-edge calibration (3xTF32 Gram), route guarded per shape.

PROFILE (trial 1) + naive fused kernel. nsys shape11: batch_trsm_left 9.0ms (2nd biggest kernel, 74% occ, 65% SM-compute-bound, 5% DRAM), potrf ~3.1ms (potrf_cta_lower_batch 74% occ + potrf_syrk_T16 71% occ/41% SM = the SYRK trailing update is the potrf bulk). Micro-bench proj_cqr substages (2b=1280,n=512,K=300): Gram 2.46ms, shift 0.61ms, potrf 2.57ms, trsm 6.39ms; FULL _sign_dc_cqr 2-pass = 22.94ms (11.9ms/pass). KEY: cuSOLVER batched potrf ALREADY at 74% occupancy (NB=16 blocked, small panels; sibling's 12.5% was the full-kxk-SMEM anti-pattern), cuBLAS trsm ALREADY 74% occ + 65% compute-bound. So the lever is FUSION removing the L HBM round-trip + separate launches, NOT occupancy. Built fused_gram_chol_trsm (Gram+Chol+tall-trsm, L resident in SMEM, 1 CTA/mat): correctness rel_err 6.8e-7 vs torch, but 162ms micro = 13.6x SLOWER (1 CTA/SM from 176KB L, 1 thread/column seq forward-sub). Routed OFF; pivot to warp-per-matrix panel design next.

WARP-PER-MATRIX batched Cholesky (right-looking, NB=16, L factored in-place in HBM, only the NB*NB diagonal block resident in SMEM -> small per-warp SMEM, wpb warps/CTA). CORRECT: rel_err 7e-8 vs cuSOLVER potrf. MEASURED SLOWER: 19.8-24.8ms across wpb in {2,4,8,16} vs cuSOLVER potrf 2.57ms = 7.7-9.6x. ncu (wpb=8, grid 160x256): Achieved Occupancy 13.7% (vs cuSOLVER potrf 74%), SM-compute 8.76% (vs cuSOLVER trailing-SYRK 41%), DRAM 1.72%, Waves/SM 0.14. Root cause is NOT SMEM (block limit shared=14) -- it's (a) grid too small at wpb=8 and (b) the per-warp serial trailing-SYRK is latency-bound (8.76% compute), which a single warp streaming O(k^2*NB) through HBM per panel cannot match cuBLAS/cuSOLVER's parallel batched-GEMM SYRK. Maps the CQR2 potrf to the LIBRARY FLOOR for this batch/K. Routed OFF (switch _FUSED_CQR_TRSM=False), benchmark parent-equal 27224us.

Warp-per-column parallelization of the FUSED trsm (each warp owns one RHS column/Q-row, 32 lanes cooperatively warp-reduce the forward-substitution dot L[i,0:i].z[0:i], nwarps=16 columns processed concurrently, L resident in SMEM). Fused Gram+Chol+trsm micro-bench: 162ms -> 70.7ms (2.3x faster than t1's 1-thread/column), correctness rel_err 5.3e-7 vs torch. Still 5.9x SLOWER than torch's split path (11.96ms): decomposed = Gram+Chol ~39ms + trsm ~32ms. Persistent wall = the full k*k L (176KB packed) forces 1 CTA/SM regardless of thread parallelism, and 512 rows / 16-concurrent-columns needs 32 serial column-batches x K=300 serial forward-sub steps. Also measured (diagnostic, reverted): INV_GEMM trsm-replacement (K*K inverse + 3xTF32 GEMM) makes shape11 WORSE (70678->108199us); right-side solve (no transpose) same as current (6.60 vs 6.38ms). Benchmark parent-equal 27236us, switch OFF.

MAPPED the CQR2 potrf/trsm to the LIBRARY FLOOR for this batch/K; no fused custom-kernel variant beat cuSOLVER+cuBLAS. Best metric = parent-equal 27208-27236us (all fused paths routed OFF; benchmark never regressed). 

PROFILING (trial 1, cited): shape-11 proj_cqr = _sign_dc_cqr 2-pass CholeskyQR2 on 2b=1280 stacked bases (n=512,K=300). Clean micro substages: Gram 2.46ms, shift 0.61ms, cuSOLVER potrf 2.57ms, cuBLAS trsm 6.39ms; one pass 11.9ms, 2-pass 22.9ms. TRSM is the biggest sub-cost. cuSOLVER batched potrf is ALREADY high-occupancy: potrf_cta_lower_batch 74% occ, trailing potrf_syrk_T16 71% occ/41% SM (the O(k^3) bulk). cuBLAS batch_trsm_left 74% occ + 65% SM-compute-bound, 5% DRAM. So the sibling's 12.5%-occ single-CTA was the anti-pattern, NOT a headroom signal -- the libraries already spread the batch at high occupancy.

BUILT + MEASURED (3 variants, all correct, all slower): (t1) full-L-resident fused Gram+Chol+trsm 1-thread/col = 162ms (13.6x); (t2) warp-per-matrix batched Cholesky (right-looking NB=16, L in HBM, small SMEM) = 24.8ms vs cuSOLVER 2.57ms (8-9x), ncu 13.7% occ / 8.76% SM (grid too small at wpb=8 AND per-warp serial trailing-SYRK is latency-bound); (t3) warp-per-column fused trsm (32-lane warp-reduced forward-sub) = 70.7ms (5.9x, 2.3x better than t1). ROOT WALL: the k=300 factor (176KB packed lower) is too big to keep resident per-matrix -> 1 CTA/SM whenever L is in SMEM; and a single warp streaming the trailing SYRK / forward-sub through HBM cannot match cuBLAS/cuSOLVER's parallel batched-GEMM SYRK+trsm. Precision was NEVER the blocker: fp32 fused Cholesky matched torch to rel_err 5e-7, orth_max ~0.0003-0.0008 vs gate 0.0055 (huge margin). Diagnostic (reverted): INV_GEMM trsm-replacement (KxK inverse + 3xTF32 GEMM) REGRESSED shape11 70678->108199us; right-side trsm (no transpose) == current.

The committed code adds 3 kernels (fused_gram_chol_trsm, warp_chol, warp-per-col trsm) all gated behind _FUSED_CQR_TRSM=False -> zero live-path change, 39/39 valid, 'stream' absent, -O3.

STILL OPEN (manager's call): (1) TENSOR-CORE trailing SYRK inside a few-warps-per-matrix Cholesky (WMMA rank-16 update) -- the one variant that could raise the 8.76%->~40% compute to challenge cuSOLVER, not yet built (large impl). (2) The trsm is 6.4ms/pass and 65% compute-bound -- attacking it needs either tensor-core reformulation (INV_GEMM tried+failed at 3xTF32) or reducing its WORK (pass-2 Gram~=I after pass-1 -> a cheaper NS/Jacobi correction, i.e. ns_refine, is brief-87 territory not this brief). (3) Launch/HBM-gap reclaim via CUDA-graph capture of the proj_cqr region (brief-103 lever) -- my isolated micro showed kernel-time ~= wall-time so the in-situ gap needs a live timeline diff to size. (4) NOT re-measured on low-rank shapes 3/4/8/10/12 (_lr_cholesky_qr2, smaller batch/k) since the fused path lost on the larger sign-DC batch; if the manager wants, a warp-per-matrix at their smaller k might behave differently. Biggest real lever remains mega_eigh_med_split_k (23.7ms = 34% of shape 11, the reduced-eigh megakernel), a DIFFERENT stage than proj_cqr.
